title: Taj Mahal
shortDescription: A marble mausoleum where symmetry, light and memory meet.
description: Commissioned by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal, the Taj Mahal was built in Agra during the seventeenth century. Its white marble changes character with the light, while its garden, calligraphy and pietra dura inlay unite architecture with poetry and craft.
keyFacts: Located on the Yamuna riverbank in Agra
Uses marble inlay called pietra dura

title: Red Fort
shortDescription: The sandstone citadel that anchored Shahjahanabad and later India’s public memory.
description: The Red Fort was begun by Shah Jahan in 1639 as the palace-fort of his new capital, Shahjahanabad. Behind its monumental walls were audience halls, gardens, water channels and private apartments that expressed imperial power through geometry and ornament.
keyFacts: The Prime Minister addresses the nation here on Independence Day

title: Akbar the Great
shortDescription: An emperor remembered for expansion, administration and experiments in pluralism.
description: Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605 and transformed the Mughal state into a durable empire. His administration combined military innovation with revenue reform, while his court sponsored translation, painting, architecture and conversations across faiths.
keyFacts: Founded Fatehpur Sikri as a capital

title: Mughal Paintings & Architecture
shortDescription: A visual language blending Persian line, Indian colour and imperial storytelling.
description: Mughal ateliers produced manuscripts, portraits and natural-history studies with extraordinary precision. Architecture followed a similarly hybrid path, bringing together Persianate planning, Timurid forms and regional Indian building traditions in gardens, tombs and palaces.
keyFacts: Manuscript painting flourished under court patronage
Natural-history studies became especially detailed under Jahangir
The style influenced later Rajasthani and Pahari schools
